title: NoAckReceiver::receive uses unsound unsafe to return aliased reference
description:
## Location
- `/Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/no_ack.rs` lines 250-253

## Problem
The `receive` method creates a shared reference via unsafe while the struct still holds a mutable reference to the same memory:

```rust
let packet = unsafe {
    core::slice::from_raw_parts(self.storage.as_ptr(), self.received_len)
};
```

The struct `NoAckReceiver<'a, ...>` holds `storage: &'a mut [u8]`. When `receive` returns a `NoAckResult<'a>` containing `Option<&'a [u8]>`, there are now two references to the same memory: the mutable reference held by the struct and the shared reference in the result.

## What Goes Wrong
If a caller:
1. Calls `receive()` and gets a completed packet reference
2. Calls `receive()` again (or any other `&mut self` method)
3. The second call mutates the storage while the first reference is still live

This is undefined behavior - the first reference points to memory being mutated through the mutable reference.

## Suggested Fix
Either:
1. Change `receive` to consume `self` when complete (prevents reuse)
2. Change the API to copy data out rather than returning a reference
3. Use interior mutability (`RefCell`) and return a `Ref<'_, [u8]>` guard
4. Make storage `&'a [u8]` (read-only) and use separate mutable state
